summary: Rapid elevation of 5xx rate during large embedding upload + priority-shed misclassification causing upstream OOMs
description:
Issue summary: Customers reported a sharp increase in 5xx responses (primarily 502/503) starting ~2026-03-13 11:45 UTC. Several dedicated customers (notably NimbleStack) saw higher error rates on embedding and streaming routes during a large bulk embedding upload. Errors correlated with upstream runtime restarts and OOM-like preemption logs.

Impact: Multiple production customers experienced request failures and increased latency for ~45 minutes. Error rate peaked at ~18% on affected routes (baseline <0.5%). Business impact for NimbleStack: failed job completions and API retries causing billing anomalies.

Environment: prod cluster in us-east (dedicated pool A, customer tenant: nimblestack-ded-1). Affects streaming and /v1/embeddings endpoints.

Observed: 5xx increase, apigw return codes 502/503, runtime processes killed and restarted with GPU OOM flag in driver logs, kvcache eviction storms, autoscaler launching ephemeral workers which then hit GPU warmup timeouts.

Expected: Stable low 5xx floor; autoscaler should add capacity without triggering rapid restarts or prefetched cache thrash.

Initial hypothesis: Large embedding upload combined with misapplied priority-shed policy caused ephemeral acceptance of many connections into a limited pool; prefetch and kvcache contended leading to runtime thrash and gpu memory fragmentation leading to OOMs and restarts.

See 'Steps to reproduce' and 'Logs' fields for reproduction notes and relevant traces.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In prod, as a dedicated tenant with high concurrency, start a large embedding bulk upload (100k vectors) in small concurrent batches.
2) Trigger a second, lower-priority streaming workload from same tenant concurrently.
3) Observe apigw return 502/503 for a subset of requests when autoscaler spins up ephemeral workers.
4) Check runtime logs for GPU allocation failures and kvcache eviction messages.

comments: 2026-03-13T12:05Z - Evelyn Park (Support): Received the alert from monitoring. Engaging SRE and customer liaison. Asking customer to pause large uploads temporarily.

2026-03-13T12:12Z - Priya Nair (SRE): Observed correlated kvcache eviction spikes and runtime restarts. Hypothesis: prefetch/pinning combined with priority-shed rule allowed too many low-priority connections to enter runtime acceptance window.

2026-03-13T12:30Z - Diego Morales (On-call Runtime): Pushed temporary rate-limit tweak on nimblestack-ded-1 to throttle concurrent embedding batches. Error rate fell to ~2% after throttling initial bursts.
2026-03-13T13:10Z - Tom Baker (NimbleStack): Confirming we paused the job and resume slowly per Support instruction. Appreciate quick mitigation. Observed job completions after throttle applied.

2026-03-13T17:45Z - Priya Nair (SRE): Follow-up: reproduced a similar error pattern in staging with synthetic load. Submitted fix PR to autoscaler backoff logic to avoid immediate ephemeral worker spin-up when kvcache eviction > threshold. See linked PRs.
investigation_notes: Checked apigw metrics: accept_queue_length spiked from 12 -> 340 coincident with embedding upload bursts.
Correlated runtime logs: repeated GPU allocation failures and fragmentation warnings between 11:46-12:30 UTC.
Replayed tenant traffic in staging: reproduces when priority-shed thresholds are mis-evaluated for mixed embeddings+streaming workload.
Verified autoscaler behavior: aggressive warmup attempts cause multiple ephemeral workers to request large KV cache prefills simultaneously, amplifying eviction storms.
Tested mitigation: applied soft throttle and increased accept window backpressure; observed errors drop and reduced runtime restarts.
resolution: Mitigation: Applied temporary tenant-level concurrency limit for nimblestack-ded-1 and added a short cooldown on autoscaler warmup attempts (10s backoff). This reduced 5xx to baseline within 20 minutes.

Permanent fix: Merged autoscaler backoff PR to gate ephemeral worker warmup if kvcache eviction rate > threshold (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4987). Updated priority-shed evaluation to consider ongoing prefetch pressure.
Rollout notes: Hotfix deployed to prod us-east on 2026-03-14 02:30 UTC behind a canary. No regression observed during canary window. Full rollout completed 2026-03-14 03:15 UTC.
Customer communication: Notified NimbleStack of mitigation and recommended best practice for large embedding uploads (partition uploads, exponential backoff).
follow_up_tasks: 1) Engineering: Add kvcache-eviction signal to autoscaler health API and expose metric to Console (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-21).
2) Product: Update docs/quickstart for embedding bulk uploads with recommended chunking patterns (owner: Maya Gupta, due: 2026-03-18).
3) SRE: Create a runbook for mixed workload priority-shed incidents and include playbook steps for temporary tenant throttles (owner: Diego Morales, due: 2026-03-17).
4) CS: Follow up with NimbleStack about billing noise and confirm no incorrect charges were applied (owner: Evelyn Park, due: 2026-03-16).
